messages.subject: Re: JRI documentation and JGR sources
messages.body_plain:
Cesar,

On Jun 28, 2007, at 1:15 PM, Cesar Martinez Izquierdo wrote:

> Hi, I want to use JRI to interface with some R packages from Java.
> However, I'm new in both R and JRI, and I'm a bit lost, so I would
> appreciate some documentation or code examples about how to perform  
> the
> following tasks from JRI:
>
> - After performing an algorithm or method in R, how to know the  
> type of
> the returned object, and how to transform it to standard Java objects.
>

The transformation is done automatically. Usually it is clear from  
the R code what the result type is, so there is no need for special  
handling.

If you really want to access the type information directly, it is  
possible. Depending on the version of the Java interface used, you  
can use is..() methods to check the type and as..() methods to coerce  
to different types (new interface) or use the getType() method (old  
interface).


> - How to inject data into R from Java in an efficient way. I want  
> to use gstat R-package, and I want to inject in R the maps that my  
> Java application has in memory (so I don't want to load the maps  
> from files with R).
>

That depends entirely on your application (and again the API you  
use). For the new API  you just use the corresponding REXPxxx  
constructors, for the old API you can either use high-level assign  
methods or you construct arbitrarily complex objects using rni...  
methods.

The examples for all tasks above are in the "examples" directory of JRI.


> I thought that probably JGR could be the best documentation for  
> such tasks, but I haven't been very successful compiling its code,  
> I think I'm not able to get the right versions:
>
> - I've downloaded sources of JavaGD 0.4-3 and rJava 0.5-0, and they
> correctly compile in my Eclipse workpsace.
> - I've downloaded JGR 1.4 sources from
> http://rosuda.org/JGR/1.4/JGRsrc-1.4.tar.gz,

Those are the release sources. You have to decide which version you  
pull, you cannot mix different versions of JRI and JGR (see below).


> and added iplots.jar
> (1.0-7). However, I get an error in JGR.java as RMainLoopCallbacks has
> changed in JRI. Where could I get the proper version of JGR sources?
> I tryied with SVN (svn co svn://svn.rforge.net/JGR/trunk JGR) but I
> could only download the R sources (not the Java sources).
>

The release versions of all above packages are on CRAN. You should  
get them either from CRAN (release versions) or from www.RForge.net  
(development versions). Combining release and development versions  
doesn't work.

As of the JGR sources, you can check them out from the RForge SVN at / 
org/trunk/rosuda/JGR

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: rjava method call
messages.body_plain:
Ron,

without actual JAR files to determine the correct signatures it is  
not possible to give you the 'correct' answer. In general, the  
strategy is to use .jmethods to find the correct argument types and  
return type and then use .jcast if necessary (i.e. if the parameter  
type is a superclass of the object). Looking at your attempt the only  
immediately visible mistake is the use of dots instead of slashes in  
the return type specification (i.e. public org.foo.Bar blah(); method  
is to be called as .jcall(o, "Lorg/foo/Bar;", "blah")).

Cheers,
Simon

I don't really understand how this automatic transformation works.
I have successfully performed a kriging using gstat R-package (using its 
example data and its tutorial):

Rengine re=new Rengine(rArgs, false, new TextConsole(this));
if (!re.waitForR()) {
	System.out.println("Cannot load R");
	return;
}
re.eval("library('gstat')");

re.eval("coordinates(meuse) = ~x+y");
re.eval("data(meuse.grid)");
re.eval("coordinates(meuse.grid) = ~x+y");

"expr" object, but I haven't been able to achieve it (I made lots of

However, I've finally managed to get the result using:
REXP exp2 = re.eval("zinc.idw$var1.pred");
double[] idwresult = exp.asDoubleArray();

messages.subject: JRI, R instances and threads
messages.body_plain:
Hi again, here there is the question I promised about JRI and threads.

I'd like to integrate R in our Java application, so that R expressions 
can be evaluated from any tools.
The idea would be that any tool/plugin in our application can get an 
REngine with a clean R environment, in which R expressions can be 
evaluated. These tools/plugins may run in parallel, in different 
threads, so several R engines may be requested at the same time.

As I told in a previous message, I'm new with JRI and also new with R, 
so I don't know anything about R threads, but I've read:
"JRI is a Java/R Interface, which allows to run R inside Java 
applications as a single thread." (from the JRI website).
Does it mean that is not possible to run several independent Rengines at 
the same time?
What will happen if I create several Rengine objets? Will they create 
several threads in the same R instance? Will they create different R 
instance? Will they have unpredictable behaviour?

Thanks for your attention, regards,

--

On Jul 3, 2007, at 1:20 PM, Cesar Martinez Izquierdo wrote:

> Simon Urbanek escribió:
>> On Jun 28, 2007, at 1:15 PM, Cesar Martinez Izquierdo wrote:
>>> - After performing an algorithm or method in R, how to know the  
>>> type of
>>> the returned object, and how to transform it to standard Java  
>>> objects.
>>>
>>
>> The transformation is done automatically. Usually it is clear from  
>> the R
>> code what the result type is, so there is no need for special  
>> handling.
>>
>> If you really want to access the type information directly, it is
>> possible. Depending on the version of the Java interface used, you  
>> can
>> use is..() methods to check the type and as..() methods to coerce to
>> different types (new interface) or use the getType() method (old
>> interface).
>
> I don't really understand how this automatic transformation works.

Every time you do an "eval" (with convert-true which is the default)  
the result is completely converted into Java objects (with the  
exception of esoteric types like environments, external pointers etc.).


> I have successfully performed a kriging using gstat R-package  
> (using its
> example data and its tutorial):
>
> Rengine re=new Rengine(rArgs, false, new TextConsole(this));
> if (!re.waitForR()) {
> 	System.out.println("Cannot load R");
> 	return;
> }
> re.eval("library('gstat')");
> re.eval("data(meuse)",false);
> re.eval("coordinates(meuse) = ~x+y");
> re.eval("data(meuse.grid)");
> re.eval("coordinates(meuse.grid) = ~x+y");
> re.eval("gridded(meuse.grid) = TRUE");

Are you sure you want to retrieve and convert all those results?  
You're discarding the Java objects anyway, so a lot of time is spent  
in conversion which you don't use anyway. You may consider using  
convert=false or even better just evaluate one expression of the form  
REXP x = re.eval("{library(...); ... zind.idw = krige(..)}")


> REX expr = re.eval("zinc.idw = krige(zinc ~ 1, meuse, meuse.grid)");
>
> Now I would expect to be able to access the kriging's result from  
> the "expr" object, but I haven't been able to achieve it (I made  
> lots of tests with the different REXP and rni methdos).
>

Sure, you can as they are all converted at this point. Note that the  
result is an S4 object, so all slots are attributes, so your example  
below would look somewhat like:

double[] idwresult = expr.getAttribute("data").asVector().at 
("var1.pred").asDoubleArray();

(see str(zinc.idw) in R for details)

However, the above will really copy everything into Java, but since  
you want only a small part of it, you should consider fetching the  
relevant parts instead, it is more efficient.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
On Jul 3, 2007, at 1:35 PM, Cesar Martinez Izquierdo wrote:

> Hi again, here there is the question I promised about JRI and threads.
>
> I'd like to integrate R in our Java application, so that R  
> expressions can be evaluated from any tools.
> The idea would be that any tool/plugin in our application can get  
> an REngine with a clean R environment, in which R expressions can  
> be evaluated. These tools/plugins may run in parallel, in different  
> threads, so several R engines may be requested at the same time.
>
> As I told in a previous message, I'm new with JRI and also new with  
> R, so I don't know anything about R threads, but I've read:"JRI is  
> a Java/R Interface, which allows to run R inside Java applications  
> as a single thread." (from the JRI website).
> Does it mean that is not possible to run several independent  
> Rengines at the same time?

Yes. R is not thread-safe, so there is no way to run multiple R  
instances in the same process. If you want a distributed client/ 
server approach, have a look at Rserve
http://www.rforge.net/Rserve/
it supports multiple parallel R processes and the client API is very  
similar to the of JRI (in fact the new API is identical so you can  
use either backend).


> What will happen if I create several Rengine objets? Will they  
> create several threads in the same R instance? Will they create  
> different R instance? Will they have unpredictable behaviour?
>

They'll crash and/or behave erratically...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I recently installed JGR on a Windows machine running R 2.5.1. I noticed
two small annoyances that seem to be related to the default .JGRprefsrc:
      * The WorkingDirectory entry contained unmasked backslashes as
        path delimiters. R complained about an "unknown escape sequence"
        or something. The delimiter should either be doubled backslashes
        or simple slashes.
      * The package grDevices isn't loaded per default. This lead to
        some problems with missing colors()-function when plotting
        networks with the network package. Maybe that's a problem with
        that specific package, but on my Linux machine grDevices gets
        loaded by default and I find this very convenient.

At least the first one should be corrected, I think. I'm not sure about
the second one. Maybe I was just used to having that package at hand
automatically.

Cheers,
Frederik

messages.subject: Re: JRI: restarting R engine
messages.body_plain:
Anya,

On Jul 11, 2007, at 10:37 AM, Anya Okhmatovskaia wrote:

> I am experimenting with using multiple instances of R in a single  
> java application. I know I cannot run more than one at the same  
> time, but I assumed I should be able to stop and restart R engine  
> consecutively. It doesn't seem to be working though.

That is true, unfortunately, because R doesn't support stopping and  
re-starting. Calling re.end() doesn't do what you think it does - it  
simply stops the thread that monitors R (depending on how you use the  
event loop), but R is still initialized and 'live'.

FWIW I don't see why you would want to re-start R. It is safe to just  
keep R running as it is idle if you're not using it, so it is much  
easier to simply accept commands sequentially and just wipe the  
global environment between calls if necessary (you could also save  
options and pars if those are relevant). If you want multiple  
parallel instances spawned very quickly, consider using Rserve instead.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: JGR and Windows Vista
messages.body_plain:
Simon, thanks for your reply. 

The author of the April post about JGR and Vista supplied me a solution, 
which (though we agree is inelegant) is sufficient for my needs.  Vista 
can run other operating systems within virtual machines, so I created a 
virtual machine, installed the OS under which I previously ran JGR, 
installed into it all the necessary components, and seemingly can run 
JGR as well as ever in the virtual machine. Performance is probably 
slower than it should be, but my needs are not that computationally 
intensive or extensive.

Vista does log debugging output, which says (obviously) that  javaw.exe 
is what crashes.  Some other technical info is in the error log though 
many of the parameters are blank.

I'm not sure how to run JGR in debug mode, in Vista.  I started it from 
a Run window, using the command "path\JGR-1.4-6.exe --debug" which led 
to the same result already observed, that being that Java crashes after 
the R console shows apparently successful loading of all the packages 
which JGR uses.  I then started R and loaded JGR from the R console but 
couldn't figure out how to run it from there in the --debug mode.  R (or 
JGR) just kept telling me that in Windows, JGR should be started using 
the aforementioned launcher.

At any rate, most anyone who needs to use JGR within Vista will likely 
be able to use the virtual machine approach, at worst.  Those who 
require higher performance are likely using a non-Microsoft environment

messages.subject: JGR 100%CPU and Upgrade on Fedora
messages.body_plain:
I installed JGR on Fedora 7 with sun java version "1.6.0_02"

Whenever it is running, it consumes 100% of one of my CPU's, all the time. 

I upgraded JGR using the JGR(update=TRUE) command from within R (attached 
below are the problems with the upgrade).

Now, when I start JGR, it (Java) still sits at 100% CPU. However If I click 
the help>about menu, and then close it, then CPU drops down to 0% after that. 
No other operation seems to cause this drop, and nothing seems to restart the 
CPU "leak". Maybe it has something to do with the splash screen at the start? 


============================
JGR Upgrade:
Installed Sun JDK, ran "R CMD javareconf", and entered "JGR(update=TRUE)" from 
within R.

Afterwords, running library(JGR) & JGR() (or running the run script) causes a 
java command help list (the list that comes up when you type java at the 
command line without any arguments)

The fix is to change the last line of the run script to be similar to the run 
script from JGR 1.4, ie, the last line:
"${JAVA}" -Djava.library.path=".:
${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}" -classpath "/usr/lib/R/library/rJava/java/boot" -Drjava.path="/usr/lib/R/library/rJava" -Drjava.class.path="/usr/lib/R/library/rJava/jri/JRI.jar:/usr/lib/R/library/iplots/java/iplots.jar:/usr/lib/R/library/JGR/java/JGR.jar" -Dmain.class=org.rosuda.JGR.JGR 
$*

becomes:
"${JAVA}" -Djava.library.path=".:
${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}" -classpath "/usr/lib/R/library/rJava/jri/JRI.jar:/usr/lib/R/library/iplots/java/iplots.jar:/usr/lib/R/library/JGR/java/JGR.jar" 
org.rosuda.JGR.JGR $*

the run script also had to be made executable (chmod 755). Then JGR can be 
started by running the script (/usr/lib/R/library/JGR/scripts/run).



--
Hope this is helpfull,
Jason Locklin
University of Waterloo
http://science.uwaterloo.ca/~jalockli
